contracts.commit_point: The _reject_foreign(request) raise immediately before handler(request) in wrap_model_call (boundary.py lines 146-148) and before await handler(request) in awrap_model_call (lines 155-157); the model call commits only if neither raise fires.
contracts.declared_mechanism: ToolBoundary.wrap_model_call and awrap_model_call call _reject_foreign(request) before the handler; _reject_foreign raises ForeignToolError when foreign_tools(request) is non-empty (any request.tools entry failing built_here) or when FOREIGN_MODEL_SETTINGS intersects request.model_settings; middleware_stack places the boundary last so it runs innermost and sees requests after any other middleware has processed them.
contracts.forbidden_condition: A model request whose request.tools contains any entry for which built_here is false (including a dict describing a provider-executed tool), or whose request.model_settings contains any key in FOREIGN_MODEL_SETTINGS — either would bind tools, servers, or betas outside the registry at the moment the model is called.

contracts.protected_operation: Each model invocation in the agent loop, with the tool bindings and model settings it would carry.
contracts.protected_resource: The outbound model request at the framework's model-call boundary — specifically its tools list and its model_settings mapping.
contracts.protection_obligation: Before every model call, any tool about to be bound to the model request must be an object blossom/tools.py built: a foreign tool object, a plain dictionary describing a provider-executed tool, or model settings containing the keys 'tools', 'mcp_servers', 'betas', or 'model_kwargs' must stop the run with ForeignToolError before the model is invoked, so nothing the registry never saw is offered to the model. (Merges both reviewer obligations covering the wrap_model_call half of the ToolBoundary.)
scope_limits: Only two request surfaces are inspected: identity of request.tools entries and presence of the four FOREIGN_MODEL_SETTINGS keys; no other channel that could influence the model call is guarded by this middleware.

Tools a model provider executes on its own side because of how the model client itself was constructed are explicitly outside this module's reach and are said to be governed by confining the client's construction, which is not among the supplied views (boundary.py lines 51-53).
The middleware trusts the package's own identity registry; it is not a defense against in-package edits to the registry or to built objects (boundary.py lines 46-49).

Ordering is load-bearing: wrap hooks compose outermost-first, so the boundary must be last/innermost via middleware_stack to observe post-processed requests; no supplied view shows the stack being consumed by an agent builder.
The guard raises before the model call and does not inspect or constrain the model's response or any subsequent turn.

contracts.protected_operation: Execution of a client-executed tool call: the handler(request) invocation inside the wrap_tool_call/awrap_tool_call hooks that runs the tool's captured function.
contracts.protected_resource: The framework tool objects built by as_langchain_tool and recorded in _BUILT_HERE (currently the single registry entry create_manual_draft) and the ALLOWED_CAPABILITIES allowlist.
contracts.protection_obligation: Every client-executed tool call must be refused before invocation unless the requested tool object is one blossom/tools.py built (object identity via built_here), its name matches the tool call's name, and its registered spec's capabilities are within ALLOWED_CAPABILITIES; a refused call returns an error ToolMessage to the model and the tool's function is never invoked. (Merges both reviewer obligations covering the wrap_tool_call half of the ToolBoundary.)
scope_limits: The check is deliberately simple — identity, name, allowlist — and does not reason about intent (boundary.py lines 25-26).

The identity registry and allowlist are trusted records of the package; the middleware is not a defense against code inside the package editing the registry, a ToolSpec, or a built object (boundary.py lines 46-49; tools.py lines 26-29).
Tools a model provider executes on its own side, and the confinement of the model client's construction said to govern them, are outside this middleware's reach (boundary.py lines 51-53).

The check bounds invocation only; what a permitted callable does before returning is bounded only by serialize_draft, which raises TypeError for any non-Draft result before it becomes a tool message — bounding what the model sees, not what the callable did (tools.py lines 19-24, 126-137).

Once any wrap_tool_call middleware is attached, the framework defers its own name check and hands the hook None for unknown names, which is why the guard requires a tool object and never trusts a name alone (boundary.py lines 35-39).

The guard is effective only where the boundary is attached via middleware_stack; no supplied view shows a construction site consuming middleware_stack() or tool_boundary, and the claimed source-scan test enforcing the ordering is not supplied.
